sentence_stem: When I was a child, I used to
correct_completion: play in the park every afternoon.
full_sentence: When I was a child, I used to play in the park every afternoon.

options.text: played in the park every afternoon.
options.why_wrong: 'Used to' must be followed by the base form of the verb, not the past form 'played'.

options.text: am playing in the park right now.
options.why_wrong: 'Used to' cannot be followed by a continuous form. It also describes the present, while the stem asks for a past habit.

options.text: play in the park every afternoon.

options.why_wrong: This describes one specific past event, not a repeated habit, and 'used to' cannot be followed by the past form 'went'.

grammar_focus: Used to + base verb for past habits
explanation: 'Used to' describes a past habit or a situation that is no longer true, and it is always followed by the base form of the verb. Turkish speakers often use a simple past tense to report past habits, so they may write a past form after 'used to' by mistake.
